question: Does the two-step claim instrument v6 (step 1 v6c sets aside background, the writer's reading, tone and words naming the reader, then sorts restatement / new claim on the trip specifics left; step 2 v6j first asks whether each listed specific is a trip specific, then judges its support) drop the false positives of the R1 fired claims and keep the stored violations, on false positives it was not shaped on?
follows: aa1048-two-step-v5 (gated run 9b0d46f8, no_go: false positives dropped 32 %, stored violations kept 95.2 %)
shaped_on_pools_note: the S279 pool file (286 held-out R1-fired claims), sha256 first 16 hex as fresh_pool writes excluded_pools; a live run needs a fresh manifest that excludes it or a train-split pool
pool: the S281 fresh pool (digest 716df551d458fee1, manifest fresh-manifest-300.json: train split, the S279 pool and the v2-v4 runs excluded), minus the claims held out below

held_out.why: v6 was written from these false positives of v5's gated run (their step votes, specifics and reasons): they are in-sample for v6 and are dropped from the pool before the subset is drawn
held_out.tp_side: the pool holds 21 stored violations and all 21 were in run 9b0d46f8; v6 was written without reading their text, specifics or reasons (aggregate counts only), so they stay the recall check of this run; a fully fresh TP side needs a new paid R1 fire and a panel round

subset: instrument_eval.select: half false positives (paraphrase, verbatim, background in proportion), half stored violations in proportion per writer, claim-hash order; after the hold-out the pool has 41 sampled false positives (paraphrase 20, background 17, verbatim 4), so a 50-claim subset takes 25 of them and every stored violation
verdict_rule: a claim is cleared when the step-1 majority is restatement; otherwise its verdict is the step-2 majority (unsupported = flagged, none = unverified); go needs every bar below

hypotheses.H1: step 1 v6c still sends >= 95 % of the stored violations on: the trip specifics they add are never set aside
hypotheses.H2: step 1 clears most background and reading false positives, because it sets them aside before it looks anything up
hypotheses.H3: step 2 v6j clears >= 40 % of the false positives it receives, because a listed specific that is not a trip specific is supported

stop_rule: one gated run; a no_go is read at $0 with the stored reasons and is never re-run on the same pool with a changed prompt
stop_rule_enforced: two_step run --limit refuses when shared.llm_call_log (stage adhoc_aa1048) holds a gated run of this id, or of the same step-1 prompt on the same pool, or cannot be read; every ledger row of a run carries prereg, run_kind and pool; v5 is a closed step set (two_step STEP_SETS) and refuses every live run
